Song Pro Horizon
A new instrument cluster for your Song Pro, with the Android Auto map and a steering wheel menu. This guide gets everything ready in a few minutes.
The Horizon theme on the cluster
Speed, power, ADAS and music in a new look, built on the car\'s own factory cluster.
The map on the cluster
With the phone on Android Auto through the app, the Waze or Google Maps map shows on the cluster.
A steering wheel menu
A wheel key opens the Horizon menu on the cluster, to change the map, the gauge and the left card.
Before you install
Song Pro Horizon is an independent project, not affiliated with BYD. Please read:
Only while parked
Install, restart the cluster and go back to factory only in P with the parking brake on. The restart turns the cluster and the head unit off for about a minute. Do not use the app while driving.
It can be undone
No system file is changed: the theme is a separate file, and the app first keeps a copy of the original cluster. Back to factory, in the Cluster section, undoes everything the app changed.
Made for the Song Pro with the 8.8\" cluster

Horizon was made and tested on head unit firmware 13.1.33.2511080.1. On other versions the app checks the cluster files before installing, but there may still be differences. If the cluster behaves oddly, go back to factory.
Before a head unit update
Go back to factory before an update, over the air or at the dealer, and install Horizon again afterwards.
Network ADB on
The app needs the head unit\'s network ADB. While it is on, another device on the same network can ask for access: only accept requests you recognise.
At your own risk
The project has no warranty and no support from BYD. You use it at your own risk.
I have read and understood the risks
Access to the head unit
The app installs the theme and turns cluster features on through the head unit itself, over local ADB, the same way DashCast and Electro do.
1. Turn network ADB on
Turn network ADB debugging on in the head unit, the same setting DashCast and Electro ask for. If you already use one of them, it is on.
2. Allow debugging
Tap Check access. The first time, the head unit asks whether to allow debugging: tick Always allow and tap Allow.
Check access
Checking… if the head unit asks, allow it.
Access granted.
No access. If the head unit asked, allow it and tap again; if it did not, turn network ADB on.
